column1: # Job 470, EN6 (Peter, 26 Nov 2026 20:07 CET, t1388u): the English rows of this draft are dropped (199
# rows: every word or form of supabase/classifier/dictionary.en.tsv, rows whose note names English, UK
# or US, and "lamp oil"); English words live in dictionary.en.tsv. Its German terms stay, so once this
# draft is accepted, point these English words at them as their concept: walnuts -> walnuss,
# hazelnuts -> haselnuss, pumpkin seeds -> kürbiskerne, maple syrup -> ahornsirup, cereal bars ->
# müsliriegel. salsa, matcha, sorbet, guacamole and pancetta are English concepts of their own now; to
# offer them in the German catalog, add them as German terms and give the English rows that concept.
# accept_drafts_test.ts checks that this draft, accepted whole, fits every language's words.
# Catalog draft, 2026-11-16, drafted by Claude (job 279, S4). Waits for human review: see catalog/REVIEW.md.
# Inputs: only supabase/classifier/*.tsv and general knowledge. No user data, no Open Food Facts, no
# Wikipedia or Commons. No allergen, nutrition or health facts. One brand, as plain text: coke.
# kind term: a dictionary.tsv row (term, category). kind synonym: a synonyms.tsv row (variant, canonical).
# Every row was probed on the local stack (supabase/classifier/probe_drafts.sh): each fixes a word the
# classifier misses or files wrongly today (gap), joins a variant to its canonical's key (key), or is a
# canonical another row needs. No word in the probe's regression set (dictionary terms, synonyms, wordlist
# and sweep words) changes category. Some compounds outside it do (probe_compounds.txt; catalog/REVIEW.md
# Job 283 (Opus review, catalog/REVIEW-opus.md) fixed 9 rows and added 23, all with source opus-review. The review cells stay
# empty for the person's review that N-215 requires.
# Order: high confidence first, then medium, then low; within each, the most common words first.
